leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members name B018 (optical lattice clocks) as their preferred single-part configuration, all with the same pair, Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. Shared: a new measurement capability based on the magic-wavelength lattice, reproduction across several laboratories, and a two-name credit that most describe as comparatively clean. Not shared: how to weigh overlap with the 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (trapped-ion control) prizes; whether the pending redefinition of the second matters; whether Ye's share is original contribution or a major improvement on Katori's concept (Olsson, Mehlig); and wording of the citation. Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig do not prefer B018 but each lists it as an alternative. Johansson, Olsson and Pearce moved to B018 after reading the openings (from first choices B008 and B003, and from B007 in Pearce's case), while Kroll and Lindroth already ranked it first, so the count partly reflects convergence after reading each other.

Eriksson alone prefers B044 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) with Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, a theory-plus-experiment structure he sees as a new state of matter. Johansson, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce each list it as an alternative. The reservations are shared across the table: unresolved pairing mechanism, a fast-moving field, and omission of first experimental authors (Cao, Fatemi) and precursor theorists. Eriksson argues that mechanism was also unsettled for cuprates; Danielsson and Lindroth weigh it the other way. Pearce raised a two-name variant (Jarillo-Herrero and MacDonald), which Eriksson rejects because it drops Bistritzer.

Mehlig alone prefers B012 (defect-mediated 2D melting, hexatic phase) for Young, Halperin and Nelson, citing mature, experimentally tested theory and clean attribution. He himself notes it has the thinnest opening support, overlaps in subject with the 2016 prize, and that first-order melting in some systems qualifies universality. He lists B018 first among alternatives and says he could move if B012 looks like a sequel to 2016. Johansson asked for more evidence on the experimental support.

Danielsson alone prefers B038 (gamma-ray burst afterglows) for Costa, Frontera and Kulkarni, as a mature discovery that resolved a thirty-year puzzle and is well confirmed by Swift and Fermi. Pearce and Mehlig agree on the science but both press attribution: optical counterpart and redshift credit (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Kulkarni's group) does not map clearly onto three names, and eligibility of some contributors is unverified. Danielsson himself concedes the attribution may sink the case and lists B018 and B004 as alternatives.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members' statements treat B018 as a serious candidate: five prefer it, and the other three (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig) list it as an alternative.

Independent reproduction and robustness across laboratories is the main shared criterion; members who prefer B018 say it is met, and members who hesitate about B044 or B007 say their evidence is thinner or still moving.

Attribution is the common obstacle: members note that a clean two- or three-name credit is rare and that B007, B038, B044 and B008 each have a credit problem that the three-name limit cannot resolve without exclusions.

The Johansson-flagged proximity to B008 means that his earlier first place for B008 is not independent evidence, and several members (Kroll, Eriksson, Danielsson, Pearce) cite the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits as a timing cost for B008.

B007 (IceCube) is regarded as important science by those who comment on it, but no member lists it in a preferred configuration, because of the three-name credit against a collaboration of hundreds and thin source-level evidence.
scientific_disputes: Whether the magic-wavelength lattice clock is a distinct discovery or a second-generation refinement of the comb (2005) and ion-control (2012) prizes. Lindroth, Johansson, Kroll and Pearce say it is a new trapping principle and a different route to stability (thousands of neutral atoms); Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson say the novelty is closer to the earlier prizes or is partly a performance record.

Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene makes the discovery immature (Danielsson, Johansson, Lindroth, Kroll in their remarks) or is irrelevant if the phenomenon is robust (Eriksson, citing cuprates).

Whether 2D melting by dislocation and disclination unbinding is universal enough for a prize given first-order melting in some systems (Mehlig's own caveat; Johansson's request for more evidence), and whether it is a sequel to the 2016 topological-transition prize.

Whether circuit QED (B008) is a distinct discovery from the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits (Johansson and Kroll argue distinct; Danielsson, Eriksson and Pearce see it as too close in time).
Whether the first-order and system-dependent melting results should lower weight on B012 compared with a laboratory discovery that has a clear before and after.
attribution_disputes: B018: Katori and Ye are accepted by all five supporters, but Olsson asks whether Ye's role is an original contribution or a better realisation, Kroll asks whether Ye's share is the accuracy and many-body work or also comb infrastructure, and Mehlig separates Katori's concept from the accuracy campaign shared with Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley and Yb and Hg groups.
B044: the three names omit Cao and Fatemi and precursor theorists (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto). Eriksson would keep Bistritzer; Pearce suggested a two-name version without him.

B038: Costa and Frontera for X-ray localisation are clear to Danielsson, Pearce and Mehlig, but optical counterpart and redshift credit (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Kulkarni's group) and eligibility of some people are unresolved.
B007: Pearce and others find three names cannot represent several hundred collaborators, and Yoshida's role is unclear.

B008: four credited names for three places, with Girvin the most-cited omission (Johansson, Danielsson, Kroll); B003 (not preferred by anyone now) has a Parkin and Butler and Mathon dispute (Olsson, Kroll, Mehlig).
maturity_disputes: Whether to wait for the redefinition of the second before recognising lattice clocks. Pearce, Olsson and Lindroth say no (accuracy has been demonstrated and reproduced); Kroll, Johansson and Danielsson raise it as a possible argument that the application is ahead of the discovery.
Whether B044 at about eight years is too early while its interpretation is moving (Danielsson, Eriksson's own caveat, Lindroth, Pearce, Johansson) or whether robust reproduction suffices (Eriksson).
B038 is regarded as mature and arguably overdue by Danielsson and Pearce, but the maturity does not settle its attribution problem.
B012 is the most mature candidate on age (more than forty years of tests), yet Mehlig acknowledges that this is offset by thin support and the 2016 overlap.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (WACQT director, Chalmers circuit-QED theorist) states he should recuse from deliberation on B008 and that his opening first place for B008 should be treated with caution.

Pearce (chair) is a member of PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations and would consider recusal from the final decision if B007 (IceCube) or B038 (GRB afterglows) is the leading candidate. He sees no specific conflict for B018, B044 or B008.

Kroll spent a year in John Hall's Boulder laboratory during his PhD (a link to the Hall-Ye environment, no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye); he says no specific conflict is apparent for B018 but would consider recusal on B023 (close to his rare-earth quantum-information work) and B008 (WACQT management team with Johansson).

Lindroth is a long-time collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and has ETH Zurich ties (Keller group) where Wallraff (B008) is based, flagged only should B008 become serious; she knows of no connection to him.

Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson share the Gothenburg physics environment; Olsson and Mehlig report no specific conflict for the shortlisted candidates. Eriksson chaired the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits, which bears on B008 but is not a personal tie. Danielsson reports no specific conflict (a scientific interest in B004 only).
questions_for_round2: For B018: what is new in the lattice clock relative to the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and can the citation state the magic-wavelength lattice and many-atom interrogation so the distinction is on the page? Do Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson find that sufficient?

For B018: is Ye's share the accuracy, coherence and many-body clock work, or does it include comb-based infrastructure, and does Olsson's rule (original experiment, not a later and better realisation) still support the pair Katori and Ye? Should Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley or Yb and Hg groups be addressed?

Should the committee wait for the redefinition of the second, or is the demonstrated 1e-18 performance and its inter-laboratory comparison already enough? Can an expert reviewer confirm the record uncertainties and comparisons (Lindroth, Pearce, Kroll)?

For B044: what in the physical picture is settled enough to write into a citation (Lindroth's question to Eriksson), how should credit for Cao, Fatemi and the precursor theory be handled within three places, and is the two-name or three-name version preferred?
Is a single-part prize for B018 the committee's intended structure, or should a two-part configuration be tested (Mehlig suggests pairing B012 with B018 or B008, at a cost in names)?

For B038 and B007: can any member name a concrete, eligible, decisive set of individuals (for B038 the optical counterpart and redshift; for B007 beyond the concept and construction), or should these be held until expert reports on attribution are available?

For B012: can Mehlig supply the experimental evidence beyond colloids and simulations for the two-step scenario (Johansson's request), and how should the first-order melting results and the 2016 overlap affect its standing?
Does B008 remain a live candidate given Johansson's recusal and the 2025 timing issue, and if so how would the four-name credit be resolved?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit preferred configurations, B018 has five of eight supporters naming the same two laureates, while B044, B012 and B038 each have one supporter, so the open questions concern whether the lattice clock is a distinct discovery rather than a successor to 2005 and 2012, whether Ye's credit is sufficient, and how to treat the pending redefinition of the second. Three of the five B018 supporters moved there after the opening, and the chair is one of them, so round 2 should test the case with the members who prefer other candidates and with expert input on the clock record, not treat the count as settled.
